requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.sources.yaml.fingerprints`.

**Obligations and the tests that cover them**

- **Comments are excluded from structural hashes.**
  - `fn[comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile]` in `src/outline/tests.rs` has a YAML case: `a.yml`, selector `pair[a]`.
  - The case changes comment text and removes a leading comment and a trailing comment. All of these must leave the hash equal.
  - It also changes a real value (`b: 1` to `b: 2`) and asserts the hash differs, so it is not trivially passing.
  - `fn[bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries]` in `tests/outline_content.rs` repeats this for YAML. An edited comment `# note` to `# edited` must leave the fingerprint equal.
- **Whitespace-separated words, with whitespace never hashed and words encoded separately.** The same test's YAML case checks `"two words"` against `"two   words"` and expects equality. It checks `"two words"` against `"twowords"` and expects inequality, which is the word-boundary distinction the requirement names.
- **SHA-256 digest.**
  - The same test asserts the fingerprint value is 64 characters, all hex digits.
  - The shared encoder is checked against known SHA-256 vectors in `src/outline/tests.rs#fn[hashes_include_grammar_kinds_nesting_and_sha256_digests]`. That test covers the empty-input vector and a tagged, length-prefixed text token, and it applies in every language.
  - That test is marked for `structural_hash` and the plain-text profile, not for YAML. The SHA-256 check lives in code shared by all languages and has no YAML-specific conditional, so the YAML tests need not repeat it.
- **Fingerprint scheme identifies the rules and version.** `fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` has a YAML case. It asserts `language.fingerprint_scheme()` and `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` equal `"yaml-structural-v1"`. It also asserts `OutlineContent::fingerprint_scheme()` on loaded content equals the language's scheme. The retention behavior itself belongs to the cited `language_provider.fingerprint_scheme` requirement, so it is not reassessed here.

**Cited requirements.** Applying `requirements.references.structural_hash` to YAML is covered by the comment-exclusion and word-boundary cases above. The cited `fingerprint_scheme` requirement is exercised through the scheme assertions.

I found no unacknowledged gap. YAML-specific edge cases the text does not name, such as block scalars containing `#`, are not required.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
Comments are excluded from structural hashes.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
